history.heading: Sahara and Sahel
paragraphs: Niger, a vast landlocked country mostly covered by the Sahara, has rich prehistoric remains, including dinosaur fossils and rock art from when the desert was green. The Aïr Mountains were home to Tuareg confederations, and Agadez, an important trans-Saharan trade city, has a historic centre listed by UNESCO.
Parts of the Songhai Empire, the Kanem-Bornu Empire and the Hausa city-states lay in Niger's territory.

history.heading: Colony and independence
paragraphs: France conquered the region in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, facing resistance including the Tuareg revolt led by Kaocen in 1916–17. Niger became independent on 3 August 1960. Military coups occurred in 1974, 1996, 1999 and 2010. Tuareg rebellions took place in the 1990s and 2000s.

history.heading: The 2023 coup
paragraphs: Mohamed Bazoum, elected in 2021 in Niger's first democratic transfer of power, was overthrown in July 2023 by the presidential guard led by General Abdourahamane Tiani. The junta expelled French and US troops, turned to Russia and joined Mali and Burkina Faso in the Alliance of Sahel States, leaving ECOWAS in 2025.

culture.heading: Peoples and traditions
paragraphs: The Hausa and Zarma-Songhai are the largest groups, along with Tuareg, Fula, Kanuri and Toubou. French was the official language until 2025, when Hausa was made the national language. About 99 percent of people are Muslim.

The Gerewol festival of the Wodaabe Fula, where young men compete in beauty contests, and the Cure Salée, a gathering of herders, are famous. Tuareg silver jewellery, such as the Agadez cross, is renowned.

politics.heading: Military rule
paragraphs: Niger is ruled by a military junta. In 2025 a transition charter set a five-year transition period, dissolved political parties and made Tiani president. Ousted president Bazoum remains in detention. Niger faces attacks by jihadist groups linked to the Islamic State and al-Qaeda.

economy.heading: Uranium and oil
paragraphs: Niger is one of the poorest countries in the world, with one of the highest birth rates. Most people depend on subsistence farming and herding, which are threatened by drought and desertification. It is a significant producer of uranium and began exporting oil through a pipeline to Benin in 2024.
The junta nationalised a major French-operated uranium mine. The currency is the West African CFA franc.
